items.title: Utah says Kalshi event contracts are illegal gambling while Kalshi says federal regulation controls, St. George Direct reports

Utah Attorney General Derek Brown announced a state lawsuit on October 20, Utah won in federal district court, and Kalshi has appealed. items.title: Connecticut judge says CFTC order does not override court reading of federal law in Kalshi prediction markets case, GambleRss reports
items.content_text: - **Connecticut judge says CFTC order does not override court reading of federal law in Kalshi prediction markets case, GambleRss reports** — GambleRss reported Judge Oliver found the CFTC order did not materially change his earlier analysis and did not show intent by the CFTC to take regulatory action against Kalshi itself, and he found no proven irreparable harm from state enforcement. items.title: Prediction markets sway voters comparable to polling, with more than 80 percent favoring stricter rules or bans, Brennan Center study via Casino.org reports
items.content_text: - **Prediction markets sway voters comparable to polling, with more than 80 percent favoring stricter rules or bans, Brennan Center study via Casino.org reports** — Casino.org reported on a Brennan Center for Justice study finding that a market-favored candidate gains a 10 to 20 percentage point boost in perceived victory regardless of polling, while low odds of 16 to 33 percent reduce perceived viability by 11 to 19 points. items.title: Canadian regulators tighten prediction market rules, barring leverage and sports contracts in the dealer model, Bonus reports
items.content_text: - **Canadian regulators tighten prediction market rules, barring leverage and sports contracts in the dealer model, Bonus reports** — Bonus reported Canadian Securities Administrators and CIRO staff published a joint notice on August 27, 2026 saying dealer-members may not allow clients to use leverage or margin on event contracts, and permitted contracts must have an initial term to maturity of 30 days or longer. The notice said sports and entertainment contracts should not be regulated within securities and derivatives legislation, CIRO staff said facilitating them was not appropriate for dealer-members, and contracts tied to elections or political events are not permitted within the dealer model. items.title: Portugal gambling regulator SRIJ orders Polymarket to halt operations after more than 4 million euros wagered on presidential election before results, GambleRss reports
items.content_text: - **Portugal gambling regulator SRIJ orders Polymarket to halt operations after more than 4 million euros wagered on presidential election before results, GambleRss reports** — GambleRss, reporting a Casino.org story published October 24, said Portugal's gambling regulator SRIJ confirmed it ordered Polymarket to halt operations because the platform is illegal under national rules that limit online gambling to licensed sports betting, casino games and horse racing, not political event markets. More than 4 million euros was wagered in a short window before election results, as Antonio Jose Seguro's implied probability rose from about 60 percent in the afternoon to about 95 percent by 6 p.m. and approached 100 percent after exit-poll projections circulated, with no evidence of insider trading reported. ([GambleRss](https://gamblerss.com/portugal-blocks-polymarket-after-e4m-election-betting-surge-54744))

items.title: Senator Ted Cruz plans post-midterm bill requiring state or tribal approval for gambling-related prediction market contracts, TheLines reports
items.content_text: - **Senator Ted Cruz plans post-midterm bill requiring state or tribal approval for gambling-related prediction market contracts, TheLines reports** — TheLines reported on October 23 that Sen. Ted Cruz plans to announce a prediction markets bill that would ban providers such as Kalshi and Polymarket from offering gambling-type contracts unless approved by a state or tribal government, shifting the decision to state governments. Genuine commodity swaps such as crops or oil would remain under federal jurisdiction, and the report said Cruz could bring the bill to committee as early as November 9 but will more likely wait until January 2027. ([TheLines](https://www.thelines.com/prediction-markets/industry-news/cruz-floats-prediction-markets-bill-to-force-state-level-oversight/))

items.title: Phantom starts staged United States launch of in-wallet prediction markets running through Kalshi, Unchained reports
items.content_text: - **Phantom starts staged United States launch of in-wallet prediction markets running through Kalshi, Unchained reports** — Unchained reported on October 23 that US users of Phantom can now trade prediction markets inside the wallet under a staged launch that began Friday and runs through Kalshi, in what Phantom called its first US integration. Users open or link a Kalshi account inside the app after identity checks, Phantom charges 0.01 dollars per contract on top of Kalshi's own 0.01 dollar exchange fee, and the product operates under CFTC Staff Letter 26-09 no-action relief granted in March, with market restrictions reported in Michigan, Nevada and Washington. ([Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/phantom-starts-a-staged-us-launch-of-in-wallet-prediction-markets/))

items.title: San Francisco 49ers lead Super Bowl LXI prediction market at 16 percent, up 2 points in a week, with Bills and Chiefs at 11 percent, DeFi Rate reports
items.content_text: - **San Francisco 49ers lead Super Bowl LXI prediction market at 16 percent, up 2 points in a week, with Bills and Chiefs at 11 percent, DeFi Rate reports** — DeFi Rate, in Super Bowl LXI prices observed October 24 at 11:43 AM ET, reported the San Francisco 49ers lead the market at about 16 percent, priced at 16 cents on Kalshi, 15.6 cents on Polymarket and 16.5 cents on Polymarket US, up 2 points over seven days. items.title: Matchbook partners with ADI Predictstreet to launch World Cup prediction market platform in the United Kingdom, Ireland and Canada, GambleRss reports
items.content_text: - **Matchbook partners with ADI Predictstreet to launch World Cup prediction market platform in the United Kingdom, Ireland and Canada, GambleRss reports** — GambleRss reported on October 24 that Matchbook has launched a FIFA World Cup-focused prediction market platform with ADI Predictstreet, its second white-label prediction market solution to go live in the United Kingdom, with availability also planned in Ireland and Canada. The offering carries yes or no markets on the World Cup winner, top scorer and in-play outcomes alongside live streaming of every match, and ADI Predictstreet is the official prediction market partner of the World Cup under a multi-year agreement with FIFA. ([GambleRss](https://gamblerss.com/matchbook-partners-with-adi-predictstreet-to-launch-world-cup-prediction-market-platform-64201))
